# Digital Hologram Numerical Reconstruction

Also called: ASM, Angular Spectrum Method, Fresnel Method

## Overview
Digital Hologram Numerical Reconstruction computes the complex wavefield at a specific depth plane from a recorded hologram matrix, effectively "refocusing" the light to visualize the 3D scene [S1]. It distinguishes itself from sibling methods by operating in the frequency domain (ASM) or using quadratic phase approximations (Fresnel) to propagate the field, rather than summing individual voxel contributions [S1].

## Shared principles
The reconstruction process begins with the loaded hologram matrix $H(x,y)$ and user-defined parameters: wavelength $\lambda$, pixel pitch $\Delta x$, and reconstruction distance $z$ [S1]. These parameters are often stored in external configuration files to avoid re-declaration [S1]. The core mechanism involves propagating the complex field from the hologram plane to the reconstruction plane. The output is typically the complex magnitude $|U(x,y)|$, which represents the intensity distribution of the reconstructed object [S1].

## Subtopics

### Angular Spectrum Method (ASM)
ASM propagates the wavefield by transforming the hologram to the spatial frequency domain, multiplying by the transfer function of free-space propagation, and transforming back [S1]. It is exact for near-field and far-field propagation, making it suitable for high-accuracy reconstruction at various distances [S1]. Choose ASM when precise phase information is required or when the reconstruction distance is small relative to the aperture size. See [Angular Spectrum Method](52-angular-spectrum-method.md).

### Fresnel Method
The Fresnel Method approximates the propagation kernel using a quadratic phase factor, assuming the paraxial approximation [S1]. It is computationally faster than ASM for large distances but less accurate for near-field scenarios or large angles. Choose this method for large reconstruction distances where computational efficiency is prioritized over exact wave optics. See [Fresnel Approximation](53-fresnel-approximation.md).

### Complex Magnitude Extraction & Histogram Enhancement
This post-processing step extracts the complex magnitude $|U(x,y)|$ from the reconstructed complex wavefield [S1]. To enhance visibility, a linear histogram stretching is applied after clipping extreme intensity values at a user-defined percentile threshold [S1]. This removes outliers and improves contrast. The user specifies the percentile value for clipping [S1]. The final result is saved as a standard PNG image [S1].

## Background
The method is implemented in tools that support multiple reconstruction algorithms, including ASM and Fresnel, configurable via external files [S1]. It is used in digital holography applications such as the reconstruction of medical datasets (e.g., B-com, EmergImg v2) and synthetic aperture holograms [S1]. The approach allows for flexible reconstruction distances and aperture sizes, as demonstrated by reconstructions at $z = 0.004$ m and $z = 0.169$ m [S1].

## Sources
